Q1: 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane is identified as a known hazard (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive effects, inhalation, oral exposure, dermal/eye contact, and organ/systemic toxicity. It also presents an expanded perspective (Tier 2) on environmental hazards, while data regarding its endocrine disruption potential are deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is included on several prominent lists of concern, such as California's Proposition 65, EPA's Drinking Water Standard, and the IARC Carcinogen list (Group 2B: possibly carcinogenic to humans). It is not found on any lists of low hazard.
Q3: 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane is very well characterized, supported by a high number of scientific references (3,332) and extensive toxicological data with 82 records in the EPA ToxValDB. Its hazard profile has been rigorously evaluated, including formal assessments by both EPA's IRIS and PPRTV programs.
